description: Bridges a decided rule dispute (seeds/rule_dispute_escalation.json) to a self-conscious-emotion appraisal (seeds/self_conscious_emotions.json) for the claim-holder who was wrong, WITHOUT editing either seed -- strictly additive. standard_met is unconditionally 0.0 -- a dispute existing at all means the claim-holder was wrong. v1.1.0 (ATTRIBUTION_LOCUS_AS_RESIDUAL_PREREG.md): attribution_locus is now a RESIDUAL, not a hand-picked lookup from the dispute outcome -- the incident's own implied signal (-1.0, standard violated) compared against the agent's held SelfPattern (0 or 1 optional edge): no pattern -> circumstance (Miller 1996's embarrassment mode, correctly recovered for first-time incidents); signs agree (confirms the pattern) -> global_self (Abramson, Seligman & Teasdale 1978's depressive attributional style); signs disagree (contradicts it) -> specific_act (Miller & Ross 1975's self-serving bias). witness_judgment stays keyed to the dispute's OWN escalate/defuse outcome (Tangney & Dearing 2002) -- a genuinely different, correctly-external signal (what OTHERS perceive), unchanged. Zero new Rust Terms -- Eq/And/IfThenElse/Count/Neighbours/PickUnique/Times/Gt/Attr/Var/Lit all pre-existed; add_node/add_edge rule effects mirror seeds/gap_awareness.json's own mint-on-decision idiom exactly. See RULE_DISPUTE_SELF_CONSCIOUS_BRIDGE_PREREG.md / _RESULTS.md and ATTRIBUTION_LOCUS_AS_RESIDUAL_PREREG.md / _RESULTS.md.

concepts.name: rule_dispute_self_conscious_bridge
concepts.definition: A rules dispute's claim-holder experiences shame, guilt, or embarrassment depending on whether the incident confirms or contradicts their own held self-pattern (a residual, not a lookup from the dispute outcome) -- while who ELSE believes a violation occurred (witness_judgment) stays keyed to the dispute's own escalate/defuse outcome, a genuinely separate signal.
concepts.why: The user asked to wire the self-conscious-emotions mechanism live off the rule-dispute escalation outcome, then to wire attribution_locus itself as a residual, mirroring issue_severity's own fix. RULE_DISPUTE_SELF_CONSCIOUS_BRIDGE_PREREG.md, ATTRIBUTION_LOCUS_AS_RESIDUAL_PREREG.md.

rules.name: bridge_dispute_to_self_conscious_context
rules.comment: PREREG Sec1: a decided RuleDisputeSignal mints a SelfConsciousContext for the claim-holder -- standard_met=0.0 unconditionally (the dispute's own premise is that this party was wrong about the rule, RULE_DISPUTE_ESCALATION_PREREG.md Sec2). attribution_locus is now a RESIDUAL (ATTRIBUTION_LOCUS_AS_RESIDUAL_PREREG.md Sec2): the incident's own implied signal vs the agent's held SelfPattern -- no pattern -> circumstance, signs agree (confirms the pattern) -> global_self, signs disagree (contradicts it) -> specific_act. witness_judgment stays keyed to the dispute's OWN escalate/defuse outcome -- a genuinely different, correctly-external signal (what OTHERS perceive), not the agent's own attribution. Guarded by a bridged_to dedup edge so re-running run_rules() does not double-mint (PREREG prediction 5).

rules.name: bridge_dispute_witness_to_self_conscious_witness
rules.comment: PREREG Sec1/prediction 4: each WitnessPresence already on the dispute's DisputeContext mints a corresponding WitnessBelief on the bridged SelfConsciousContext, judgment taken from the SAME witness_judgment Rule 1 already derived (not re-derived here) -- an escalated (public, confrontational) dispute reads to onlookers as a clear violation; a defused one does not. Guarded by a mirrored_as dedup edge per witness (PREREG prediction 5).
